
=================================================================
#25 Chunchu & Yeon  (642 October)
Arc: Iron Will · place: pyongyang · tone: enemy-parley thriller
Logline: To save Silla, Chunchu has to walk into Pyongyang and ask the most dangerous man in Samhan for a favour.
=================================================================
[0] ¶ Every morning since Daeya, Chunchu asks the Queen for the same thing. Every morning she says no.
[1] ¶ He wants to go north to Pyongyang and borrow an army against Baekje. Then news comes down from the north, a month late, the way it always does.
[2] Queen Sunduk: What…! The King of Goryeo, murdered by his own subject?
[3] Kim Yushin: Well I never… I thought our country would fall first, and Goryeo goes ahead of us. So who is this subject?
[4] Alchun: They call him the Eternal General — Yeon, or Gesomun. Commoners say Red Sun of Pyongyang when they think courts cannot hear.
[5] King Muyeol: “Yeon Gesomun”…
[6] Queen Sunduk: A man who kills his own king at a banquet. / And you want to go and ask him for a favour.
[7] King Muyeol: A man like that is the only kind who can still say yes, Majesty. / Everyone else has to ask a council.
[8] Queen Sunduk: And what will it cost?
[9] King Muyeol: Only me. I’m cheap.
[10] Queen Sunduk: Nothing you do is cheap, Chunchu. / …Go. Before I think of a better question.
[11] ¶ The Queen lets him go. Nobody offers to go instead.
[12] Kim Yushin: If you go and do not return, my white horse will trample Goryeo underfoot without fail.
[13] King Muyeol: I will return within sixty days. If I have not returned by then, there will be no promise of meeting again.
[14] ── SCENE: The West Gate ──
[15] ¶ He leaves by the west gate of the Moon Palace on **Hadong**, a lean red bay he named for summer and winter, because a diplomat’s horse, he says, has to stand in both. Yushin walks beside the bridle as far as the gate and no farther, which for Yushin is a speech.
[16] [MAP 642: Sixty days there and back, through a country that has just killed its own king. He packs light.]
[17] Kim Yushin: Sixty days. / He knows the way back. Even if you forget.
[18] King Muyeol: You’re saying he’s smarter than me. / …Hear that, Hadong? Yushin trusts you.
[19] Kim Yushin: It’s you I don’t trust.
[20] ── SCENE: Pyongyang ──
[21] ¶ Pyongyang lets him in through the red gate and keeps him waiting on the stair. When someone finally comes down, it is Dosuryu, the Grand Herald.
[22] King Muyeol: Your Excellency…
[23] ¶ Chunchu requests to see the king.
[24] ¶ **King Bojang** makes his request — though the word _his_ is doing generous work, and everyone in the room knows for whom.
[25] ¶ The price is simple. Give back the passes Silla took.
[26] Yeon Gesomun: Oi, Silla — why the long face?
[27] Yeon Gesomun: And call it Goguryeo. / Not Goryeo. I am not tired enough to shorten my own country.
[28] King Muyeol: Goguryeo, then — if the chronicles insist. / Most men I meet have already shortened it.
[29] King Muyeol: You would take this land’s crisis as your chance, and demand territory? / As a subject I have no say, so I await your judgement. And now — I take my leave…
[30] Yeon Gesomun: You come into another man’s house, refuse his price, and still look me in the eye. / Has Silla no pride left? Or is it only you?
[31] King Muyeol: I know no such thing as pride. / Pride is a decoration for men who can afford to lose. / I know where I am going. There is nothing in this room large enough to stand in the way.
[32] Yeon Gesomun: …
[33] ¶ Outside the door, two Goguryeo soldiers have been listening the way soldiers listen — professionally, and for sport.
[34] Gate Guard: Did you hear him? / …Said it to the Mangniji’s face. Didn’t blink once.
[35] Junior Guard: Silla men talk like that when they want to walk into Yumla’s court stylishly.
[36] Gate Guard: Bet you a dried fish he crawls out on his knees.
[37] Junior Guard: Bet you two he cries.
[38] ¶ The door opens. **Chunchu** is escorted out between two attendants. His left hand is a red glove. Blood runs off the wrist and dots the stone like a trail someone meant to follow.
[39] Junior Guard: …Ah?
[40] Gate Guard: Ah——??
[41] Junior Guard: Why is there blood. By the Holy King’s bow, why is there so much blood.
[42] Gate Guard: Did—— did the Mangniji cut him?
[43] Dosuryu: Move. Prison.
[44] Junior Guard: Prison? The man brushed past the death escort and he still has that face on.
[45] ── SCENE: The Cell ──
[46] ¶ They put him in a cell with a window. That is meant to be a courtesy. The courtesy does not include a physician.
[47] King Muyeol: (…Good. He looked. He will remember looking.)
[48] ¶ What the guards do not know — what nobody in the corridor knows — is whose blade opened the hand. That answer waits in another man’s memory, for another meeting.
[49] ¶ Chunchu has no physician, but he has a sleeve, and sewn into it is what a Silla envoy carries when he expects to be robbed. Somehow it reaches **Seon Dohae**, the king’s favourite, without passing through any door the Mangniji is watching.
[50] ❝QUOTE (Samguk Sagi (三國史記) bk. 41, Biographies — Kim Yushin; Lee Byong-do ed., vol. 2 (Chunchu in Goguryeo, 642)): Chunchu secretly gave three hundred measures of blue cloth to the king’s favourite, Seon Dohae.❞
[51] ¶ Seon Dohae arrives with a jar of wine and no guards, which is either courage or an arrangement. He pours two cups, drinks both when Chunchu does not reach for his, and starts talking about the sea.
[52] Seon Dohae: Can’t hold a cup with a hand like that. I’ll drink it for you. / …Tell me, my lord. Ever heard the one about the turtle and the rabbit?
[53] King Muyeol: …Even if I had, I’d like to hear it from you.
[54] Seon Dohae: The Dragon King of the Eastern Sea had a daughter with a sick heart. The physician said a rabbit’s liver would cure her. / No rabbits in the sea. So the turtle climbs up on land and strikes up a conversation with a rabbit. / “Out in the middle of the sea there’s an island. Clear water, fruit everywhere, no hawks, no eagles. Come on. Get on my back.”
[55] King Muyeol: And the rabbit got on.
[56] Seon Dohae: Got right on. The Holy King ran across a river on turtles’ backs, so turtles are generally trustworthy. Generally. / Two or three li out, the turtle turns his head and confesses. Actually, we need your liver. / And do you know what the rabbit said?
[57] King Muyeol: …
[58] Seon Dohae: “Oh dear. I’m descended from spirits, I can take out my insides and wash them. My chest’s been tight lately, so I left my liver drying under a rock. Let’s go back and fetch it.” / The turtle believed him and turned around. The moment they touched the shore, the rabbit was into the grass. / “Idiot. Who lives without a liver?”
[59] ¶ Seon Dohae refills his own cup and looks at nothing in particular. Chunchu looks at his ruined hand for a long time, then laughs once, quietly, the way a man laughs when a lock he has been picking turns over.
[60] King Muyeol: …Could I trouble you for paper? / The left one’s in no state, so I’ll use the right.
[61] ¶ The letter goes to the king, not the Mangniji. The passes were Goguryeo's to begin with, it says, and once Chunchu is home he will ask his sovereign to give them back. He signs with a flourish. He has no intention of doing any such thing. His drinking partner, finishing the jar, has no intention of mentioning it.
[62] ── SCENE: Surabol ──
[63] ¶ On the sixtieth day **Yushin** starts counting out men. He does not ask the Queen first.
[64] ── SCENE: The Mangniji’s Desk ──
[65] ¶ In Pyongyang, Dosuryu brings Yeon two pieces of paper on the same morning. One is the envoy’s letter to the king. The other is a scout’s report from the border.
[66] Dosuryu: The letter says he’ll ask his queen to give back the passes. / He won’t, of course. / This one says ten thousand Silla men are camped at the border. With a white horse at the front.
[67] Yeon Gesomun: …What? The Sword of the Divine Country is coming? / …Let him go.
[68] Dosuryu: Sir?
[69] Yeon Gesomun: Did you not hear me? Release Chunchu. / But truly… who is this Chunchu — the most cunning man in Samhan — that the Sword of Silla comes for him himself?
[70] Dosuryu: Who is this Sword of Silla, that the Eternal General jumps like this? / Don’t tell me… you’re afraid?
[71] Yeon Gesomun: Old man— even a man ready to die does not poke a tiger for no reason. / The day will come when we face Yushin… / but not over something like Chunchu.
[72] Yeon Gesomun: Keep the letter. / He signed it. One day I’ll make him read it back to me. / That’s the win.
[73] ── SCENE: The Border Camp ──
[74] ¶ On the Silla side of the border, in a camp that should not exist, Yushin has brought the horse. Hadong is tied at the front of the lines with an empty saddle, the way some armies carry an empty chair. When Chunchu comes down the last hill on foot, thinner, the left hand bound against his chest, the horse sees him before the men do.
[75] King Muyeol: …Hadong. / You got fat. Yushin fed you better than they fed me.
[76] Kim Yushin: Hand. / …Give it here. The right one.
[77] ¶ Chunchu cannot close the left hand on a rein, so Yushin ties both reins around his right wrist himself, in a knot he learned in the drill yard for men who have been shot. He says nothing about the hand, and Chunchu says nothing about the camp.
[78] King Muyeol: They opened my door the morning your camp appeared. No reason given.
[79] Kim Yushin: Perhaps he heard I was coming.
[80] King Muyeol: (…A more fearsome man than I expected. Both of them.)
[81] [MAP 642: One envoy coming south, ten thousand Silla men coming north, and a border between them that has gone very polite.]
[82] ¶ **One envoy left Pyongyang bleeding. Whose blade was it? Now the King of Baekje walks in on purpose, laughing…!**
